text.en: A young seagull stands alone on a ledge, hungry, afraid to take the leap that every bird must take.

The young seagull is the only one in his family who has not flown. His brothers and sister have already left the ledge and his parents have scolded and threatened him, but he is too frightened of the long drop to the sea. After a day without food he sees his mother holding a piece of fish just out of reach, and in hunger he dives at it.
He falls, then finds his wings and soars. His fear disappears and the whole family flies around him. The story shows that fear is often conquered only by trying and that a push, even a harsh one, can help us find our strength.
Words to learn: ledge, precipice, plateau, plaintively and soar. The author uses detailed description of the bird's feelings so that we sympathise with him.
